synopsis: RTCA and EUROCAE are identified as aviation standards bodies that published ACAS X minimum operational performance standards DO-385 and ED-256 in October 2018 [f15747, f15371]. Chapter 2 describes ACAS X acceptance as proceeding through their standards and aviation authorities, consistent with the glossary’s account of aircraft collision-avoidance validation acceptance [f1434, f15753]. Chapter 2 also states that RTCA, EUROCAE, and aviation authorities accepted ACAS X evidence [f1912]. These facts establish an aviation acceptance precedent, but do not specify an RTCA acceptance route or timeline for heavy off-road braking systems [f1434, f1912, f15747, f15371, f15753].

relations.note: Both describe acceptance through RTCA and EUROCAE standards and aviation authorities.
Both identify DO-385 and ED-256 publication by RTCA and EUROCAE in October 2018.
Identifies evidence acceptance by the bodies involved in the standards-based acceptance route.
Names and dates the ACAS X standards associated with the acceptance route.
Reported evidence acceptance supports the glossary’s account of validation acceptance.
